profile.implementation: Offline Linux-oriented upstream-manual/kernel-documentation profile; no installed build claim
startingSummary: Provisioned client with independent outbound Alice identity
Alice cached TGT; separate machine keytab; nfs service key stays server/KDC
Explicit server export, principal mapping and file policy
assumptions: Fixed clock and synthetic fixtures; no runtime network or crypto implementation
No delegation, pNFS, COPY, GSSv3 or NFS14
Machine-state proof does not grant user file access
POSIX-mode/group fixture separate from NFSv4 ACE semantics; AD lookup is a declared local adapter
RFC8881 clients MUST support krb5/krb5i and SHOULD support krb5p; servers MUST support all three. Configured sec is independent of required implementation support; v4.2 does not enable TLS by itself.
transports: Kerberos TGS to KDC TCP88; not per READ
profile.completion: Client accepts request-specific bytes only after receiver-local protection, state, mapping, export and file checks; denials preserve unrelated state.
algorithms: Distinct ticket session, initiator subkey and acceptor per-message key
profile.cryptoDetail: All crypto values/verdicts are SYM/HANDLE. GSS header MIC covers RPC header through credential; body protection covers XDR(sequence||arguments/results); krb5 does not protect body. TLS secrets and GSS context keys are distinct local objects.

profile.implementation: Offline Linux-oriented upstream-manual/kernel-documentation profile; no installed build claim
startingSummary: Provisioned client with independent outbound Alice identity
Alice cached TGT; separate machine keytab; nfs service key stays server/KDC
Explicit server export, principal mapping and file policy
assumptions: Fixed clock and synthetic fixtures; no runtime network or crypto implementation
No delegation, pNFS, COPY, GSSv3 or NFS14
Machine-state proof does not grant user file access
POSIX-mode/group fixture separate from NFSv4 ACE semantics; AD lookup is a declared local adapter

transports: Kerberos TGS to KDC TCP88; not per READ
profile.completion: Client accepts request-specific bytes only after receiver-local protection, state, mapping, export and file checks; denials preserve unrelated state.
algorithms: Distinct ticket session, initiator subkey and acceptor per-message key

startingSummary: Nonjoined workstation/alex with independent outbound Alice identity

profile.name: NFS-WINDOWS2025-R1
profile.publicationStatus: Published RFC baseline; rfc8881bis draft is not normative replacement
profile.supportStatus: Standards/manual-backed, native build and interoperability unverified
profile.implementation: Linux client to Windows Server2025 NFSv4.1; configured AD lookup; server role/share/SPN prerequisite
startingSummary: Provisioned client with independent outbound Alice identity
Alice cached TGT; separate machine keytab; nfs service key stays server/KDC
Explicit server export, principal mapping and file policy
assumptions: Fixed clock and synthetic fixtures; no runtime network or crypto implementation
No delegation, pNFS, COPY, GSSv3 or NFS14
Machine-state proof does not grant user file access
POSIX-mode/group fixture separate from NFSv4 ACE semantics; AD lookup is a declared local adapter
RFC8881 clients MUST support krb5/krb5i and SHOULD support krb5p; servers MUST support all three. Configured sec is independent of required implementation support; v4.2 does not enable TLS by itself.
transports: Kerberos TGS to KDC TCP88; not per READ
profile.completion: Client accepts request-specific bytes only after receiver-local protection, state, mapping, export and file checks; denials preserve unrelated state.
algorithms: Distinct ticket session, initiator subkey and acceptor per-message key
profile.cryptoDetail: All crypto values/verdicts are SYM/HANDLE. GSS header MIC covers RPC header through credential; body protection covers XDR(sequence||arguments/results); krb5 does not protect body. TLS secrets and GSS context keys are distinct local objects.
